principles.title: Don’t drift from the color tokens
principles.description: No hardcoded color — use the token utilities.
principles.rationale: Color must flow through the token layer so it themes per context. AGENTS.md: never a generic Tailwind palette (text-slate-*), hex, or bg-white. The gray/primary/secondary ramps ARE tokens (src/index.css scales), so gray-* passes.
principles.fix: Use bg-background / text-foreground / text-muted-foreground, the semantic triad (success / neutral / destructive), gray-*, or a gradation step (primary-1…5 / secondary-1…5).

principles.title: Color modulation steps on the gradation scale
principles.description: Tints and shades of brand families come from gradation steps (primary-1…5 / secondary-1…5) — not ad-hoc alpha or color-mix.
principles.rationale: Stepping between authored values is what makes UI read as done, organized, trustworthy — the same discipline as the 8-grid, applied to color. Founder (2026-08-21): “You should be stepping between values on the ramp by default… A brand could then define their own versions of it, but MVDS should be opinionated about it being there.” Steps carry role contracts (1–2 tint surfaces, 3 decorative, 4–5 text-safe) that check:contrast enforces; an ad-hoc /10 alpha carries no contract at all.
principles.fix: Pick a gradation step by role: bg-primary-1/-2 for tint surfaces, -3 for decorative borders/gradients, text-primary-4/-5 for text. See the Foundations/Color specimen.
principles.docs: AGENTS.md (Golden rules — Color via tokens; Spacing — the 8 grid for the stepping idea)

principles.title: Typography size steps on the semantic ramp
principles.description: Type sizes come from the semantic ramp (text-display … text-caption) — never generic size utilities or arbitrary sizes.
principles.rationale: The prose golden rule (“never ad-hoc text-2xl font-bold”) becomes data. Each ramp step carries the whole spec (size + line-height + weight + tracking), so stepping keeps hierarchy consistent everywhere an agent or human sets type.
principles.fix: Use a semantic ramp step: text-display, text-h1…text-h4, text-body-lg, text-body, text-small, or text-caption.
principles.docs: AGENTS.md (Golden rules — Type via the semantic ramp)

principles.title: Space siblings with gap, not margins
principles.description: No margins for spacing — space siblings via the parent primitive's gap.
principles.rationale: Spacing is one number in one place (the parent's gap). AGENTS.md: the only sanctioned margin is mx-auto to center a Container.
principles.fix: Remove the margin; wrap siblings in <Stack gap> / <Inline gap> / <Grid gap>. To center a Container, mx-auto is allowed.
principles.docs: AGENTS.md (Golden rules — Gap is the ONLY way to space siblings)

principles.title: Layout only via Stack / Inline / Grid
principles.description: No raw flex/grid layout utilities outside the layout primitives.
principles.rationale: Layout is owned by Stack/Inline/Grid. AGENTS.md: never raw flex/grid utilities for layout.
principles.fix: Use a layout primitive: <Stack>/<Inline> (flex) or <Grid> (grid) from src/components/layout.
principles.docs: AGENTS.md (Golden rules — Never raw flex/grid utilities for layout)

principles.title: Every UI component has a story
principles.description: Every UI component has a co-located *.stories.tsx.
principles.rationale: Storybook is the verification gate. AGENTS.md: one story file per UI component.
principles.fix: Add a co-located *.stories.tsx enumerating every variant/state in light + dark.

principles.title: Every site section has a story
principles.description: Every site section component has a co-located *.stories.tsx.
principles.rationale: Storybook is the verification gate for site/ sections (the landing-page surface) exactly as for ui/ components.
principles.fix: Add a co-located *.stories.tsx exercising the section in light + dark.

principles.title: Layout family covered in one story
principles.description: Every layout primitive is covered by the shared layout story.
principles.rationale: AGENTS.md: a cohesive primitive family may share one story (layout.stories.tsx) rather than one per file.
principles.fix: Cover the primitive in src/components/layout/layout.stories.tsx (the shared family story).
principles.docs: AGENTS.md (Storybook — a cohesive primitive family may share one story)

principles.title: Blocks family covered in one story
principles.description: Every content block primitive is covered by the shared blocks story.
principles.rationale: AGENTS.md: a cohesive primitive family may share one story (blocks.stories.tsx) rather than one per file.
principles.fix: Cover the primitive in src/components/blocks/blocks.stories.tsx (the shared family story).
principles.docs: AGENTS.md (Storybook — a cohesive primitive family may share one story)

principles.title: Show real status, don’t claim it in prose
principles.description: The system tells you what it knows about itself, in time to matter.
principles.rationale: The reason this landing page reports gate results and sync state rather than claiming quality in prose. A drifted mirror or a failing check should be legible at a glance and distinguishable from the expected state — which is why the status triad separates 'trailing by design' from 'genuinely disagrees'.
principles.fix: Surface real state from a generated source. Never hand-write a status that could go stale without anything failing.

principles.title: Speak the user’s world
principles.description: The surface speaks the reader's language — words, flows, and objects match how the work actually happens.
principles.rationale: Why primitive props take pixels and tokens speak roles — the system's names mirror the designer's intent, not the implementation's units.
principles.fix: Name things for the reader's job, not the implementation. If a prop, label, or token needs translating before use, rename it.
principles.docs: AGENTS.md (Golden rules — Type via the semantic ramp)

source.name: Nielsen Norman Group
source.ref: Heuristic 2: Match between system and the real world

principles.title: Every path has an exit
principles.description: No dead ends: actions can be undone, escaped, or backed out of without penalty.
principles.rationale: Why suppressions are explicit and visible (mvds-allow), and why pre-1.0 removals are clean breaks — no state you cannot see your way out of.
principles.fix: Provide the way out: make suppressions visible (mvds-allow), removals clean, and every state escapable.

principles.title: One concept, one expression
principles.description: One concept, one expression — a thing that behaves the same should look the same everywhere.
principles.rationale: This is the whole argument for a token layer and a fixed variant set. Every ad-hoc value is a second dialect a reader has to learn, and an agent has to guess between. The mechanical half is enforced (no-hardcoded-color, no-raw-flex-grid); the judgment half is deciding when a genuinely new case deserves a new variant instead of a one-off.
principles.fix: Before adding a variant or a bespoke style, find the existing expression of the same idea and reuse it. If none fits, add it to the system rather than to the screen.

principles.title: Make the wrong thing hard to type
principles.description: Make the wrong thing impossible to express, rather than catching it later.
principles.rationale: Why primitive props are typed to the 8-grid: gap={12} is a compile error, not a review comment. Prevention beats detection beats documentation, in that order — the principles gate and the edit-guard hook exist for the cases the type system cannot reach.
principles.fix: Prefer a narrowed type or a constrained prop over a lint rule; prefer a lint rule over a line in the docs.

principles.title: Names that mean what they say
principles.description: Names should say what they mean, so nobody has to hold a mapping in their head.
principles.rationale: Why the type ramp is semantic (text-h1, not text-2xl font-bold) and why primitive props take pixels (gap={16}, not gap-4 meaning 16px). A name that must be translated before use is a name that will be used wrongly — by a person at 5pm, and by an agent every time.
principles.fix: Name for the intent, not the implementation. If a value needs a comment to explain what it maps to, the name is wrong.
principles.docs: AGENTS.md (Golden rules — Type via the semantic ramp)

principles.title: Fast for experts, obvious for first-timers
principles.description: Accelerators exist for the practiced hand without hiding the plain path.
principles.rationale: Why the primitives are few and composable: the expert path and the beginner path are the same path, just faster.
principles.fix: Add the accelerator beside the plain path, never instead of it — one vocabulary, two speeds.

source.name: Nielsen Norman Group
source.ref: Heuristic 7: Flexibility and efficiency of use

principles.title: Cut surface that doesn’t earn its place
principles.description: Every element competes for attention with every other one — so carry no surface you cannot justify.
principles.rationale: Why the component set is deliberately tiny and why pre-1.0 MVDS deletes rather than deprecates. Unused variants are not free: they dilute the signal of the ones that matter and enlarge the space an agent chooses from.
principles.fix: Cut it. If a variant, prop, or export is not earning its place, remove it outright — there are no external consumers to protect yet.

principles.title: Errors say what to do next
principles.description: An error names the problem in plain language and carries its own fix.
principles.rationale: Why every manifest record carries a fix: line — the gate that fails you also tells you the way out.
principles.fix: When you author a failure message, include the fix — a gate that only says no is half a gate.
principles.docs: AGENTS.md (Before you call a change done)

source.name: Nielsen Norman Group
source.ref: Heuristic 9: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors

principles.title: Help lives where the work happens
principles.description: Guidance is co-located with the task — searchable, concrete, and short.
principles.rationale: Why stories are co-located and autodocs generated — documentation that lives beside the code it documents cannot drift far.
principles.fix: Put the guidance where the work happens: co-located stories, autodocs, and comments that state constraints.
